classification.difficultyReason: Substitute sales quantities into two supplied linear functions, compare revenue with cost, and equate the functions to find break-even; the required model and interpretation are directly supplied.

content.prompt:
A company sells a product for $\$50$ per unit. The cost to produce $x$ items is given by the cost-function
$$C(x)=200+10x.$$
The revenue-function
$$R(x)=50x$$
models the gross revenue from selling $x$ units.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the cost and revenue after selling 2 units? Has the company made profit yet?

answer.short: Cost: $\$220$; revenue: $\$100$. No; the company has made a loss of $\$120$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C(2)&=200+10(2)\\C(2)&=220\\R(2)&=50(2)\\R(2)&=100\end{align*}$$
The cost is $\$220$ and the revenue is $\$100$. Revenue is $\$120$ below cost, so the company has made a loss.

answer.short: Cost: $\$300$; revenue: $\$500$. The company has made a profit of $\$200$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}C(10)&=200+10(10)\\C(10)&=300\\R(10)&=50(10)\\R(10)&=500\end{align*}$$
The cost is $\$300$ and the revenue is $\$500$. Revenue exceeds cost by $\$200$, so the company has made a profit.

children.label: c
children.prompt: How many units does the company need to sell in order to have a profit of zero dollars, i.e., break even?

answer.worked:
At break-even, revenue equals cost:
$$\begin{align*}50x&=200+10x\\40x&=200\\x&=5.\end{align*}$$
The company breaks even after selling 5 units.
